title: Specific Motivational Interviewing Questions for Diabetes Self-Management
implementation_guidance: Use these specific motivational interviewing questions during patient encounters: 1) "What concerns you most about your diabetes?" 2) "On a scale of 1-10, how important is it for you to change [specific behavior]?" 3) "Why did you choose that number and not a lower one?" 4) "What would it take to move you from a [current number] to a [higher number]?" 5) "What are the good things about changing this behavior?" 6) "What are the not-so-good things about changing this behavior?" 7) "What has worked for you in the past when you've tried to make a change?" 8) "What specific steps do you feel ready to take in the next week?"
expected_outcomes: Increased patient engagement in self-management, improved intrinsic motivation for behavior change, better adherence to treatment plans, enhanced patient-provider communication, reduced resistance to change, and improved glycemic control through patient-centered goal setting.
target_population: Medicaid-enrolled individuals with type 2 diabetes, particularly those struggling with behavior change or medication adherence.
citation: Stuckey HL, Dellasega C, Graber NJ, Mauger DT, Lendel I, Gabbay RA. Diabetes Nurse Case Management and Motivational Interviewing for Change (DYNAMIC): Study Design and Baseline Characteristics in the Chronic Care Model for Type 2 Diabetes. Contemp Clin Trials. 2009;30(4):366-374. doi:10.1016/j.cct.2009.03.002.
